label: caiso 12 ixexport only
definition: KEEPER (strict improvement over caiso-10 baseline). New --interchange-shaping-export-only: shapes ONLY the export side of the priced node (force/cap midday export to the measured EIA-930 envelope) and leaves every import tranche available every hour. This isolates the GOOD half of caiso-11's full shaping (the midday-export cap, which saturates and forces surplus to curtail renewables at -$20 -> negative prices) from the BAD half (the gross-import-availability cap, which conflated net vs gross and starved baseload imports -> gas blowup). RESULT: unlocks the SAME negative midday hours as full shaping (2023: 12 hrs min -$20; 2025: 1 hr) while keeping the generation mix and mean LMP BYTE-IDENTICAL to baseline — 2024 gas 70.9 (vs caiso-11's 85.0; EIA-923 67.7), import 32.2 (vs 17.4; actual 32.4), LMP mean $54.2 (vs 11's $61.4). Zero mix/level cost for the negative tail. REMAINING GAP: the magnitude is small (2024 still 0 neg hrs; min only -$20 vs actual -$58; mean still $54 vs ~$33) because imports stay FLAT (uncapped) and absorb the midday surplus the real grid cannot. The model isn't long ENOUGH midday at the correct 0.80 gas floor. NEXT-BEST KNOB: a TOTAL-PRESERVING gross-import diurnal shape (back imports off midday without cutting the daily import level) so the model can't lean on flat imports to dodge curtailment — the priority-2 import-realism work; this export-only keeper is the clean foundation for it. (caiso-13 brackets the gas-floor-depth sensitivity as a probe.)
